Hydrosphere Theory

Scope, process inventory, and certificate map

The RELIC hydrosphere domain (relic.scientific.hydrosphere) governs land-surface evapotranspiration, snowpack mass-energy balance and snow-aging albedo, van Genuchten soil-water retention, single-bucket and vertical Richards vadose-zone moisture dynamics, infiltration- and saturation-excess surface runoff, hybrid event-triggered Hortonian surface ponding, subsurface lateral stormflow, vadose-aquifer percolation and capillary exchange, and unconfined groundwater storage (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 19).

Fourteen concrete scientific Functors reside in relic.scientific.hydrosphere, each paired with an IPHSEquivalenceCertificate spanning Level 1 through Level 3 (2 at Level 1, 2 at Level 2, and 10 at Level 3). A related vadose-zone solver, SoilWaterTransportFunctor (Level 3), resides in relic.scientific.pedosphere.transport and is contrasted below to enforce single-writer soil_moisture governance.

General conservation rules follow Mathematical Foundations, discrete cochain operators follow DEC, IPHS, and GENERIC, and hybrid event semantics follow Numerical Methods.

Evapotranspiration closures

Penman-Monteith combination equation

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.evapotranspiration.penman_monteith.PenmanMonteithET (Level 3) combines surface energy balance with aerodynamic and surface-resistance vapor transfer (Monteith, 1965; Allen et al., 1998). With available radiative energy \(A_e = R_n - G\) [W m\(^{-2}\)], saturation vapor-pressure slope \(\Delta = \frac{\mathrm{d}e_s}{\mathrm{d}T}(T_a)\) [Pa K\(^{-1}\)], psychrometric constant \(\gamma = \frac{c_p P}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mw}}\lambda_v}\), vapor pressure deficit \(D = \max(e_s(T_a) - e_a, 0)\) [Pa], aerodynamic resistance \(r_a\), and bulk surface resistance \(r_s\), latent heat flux \(\lambda_v E\) [W m\(^{-2}\)] and mass evapotranspiration flux \(E_{\mathrm{ET}}\) [kg m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\)] satisfy

\[ \lambda_v E = \frac{\Delta(R_n - G) + \rho_a c_p D / r_a}{\Delta + \gamma\left(1 + r_s / r_a\right)}, \qquad E_{\mathrm{ET}} = \frac{\lambda_v E}{\lambda_v}. \]

Canopy interception evaporation, plant transpiration, and bare-soil evaporation are partitioned consistently with canopy cover fraction and root-zone moisture availability without mutating soil water directly.

Priestley-Taylor equilibrium-radiation closure

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.evapotranspiration.priestley_taylor.PriestleyTaylorET (Level 3) evaluates equilibrium evaporation scaled by the Priestley and Taylor (1972) advection coefficient \(\alpha_{\mathrm{PT}}\) (typically \(1.26\) for well-watered surfaces) and soil-moisture stress scalar \(\beta_W \in [0, 1]\):

\[ \lambda_v E_{\mathrm{pot}} = \alpha_{\mathrm{PT}}\,\frac{\Delta}{\Delta + \gamma}\,(R_n - G), \qquad E_{\mathrm{ET}} = \beta_W\,\frac{\max(\lambda_v E_{\mathrm{pot}}, 0)}{\lambda_v}. \]

In any composed simulation graph, either PenmanMonteithET or PriestleyTaylorET is selected as the sole writer of evapotranspiration_flux.

Snowpack mass-energy balance and snow albedo

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.snow.snowpack.SnowPack (Level 3) maintains a coupled mass-and-cold-content ledger for snow water equivalent \(W_{\mathrm{snow}}\) [kg m\(^{-2}\)] and snow internal thermal state (Anderson, 1976; Tarboton and Luce, 1996). Total precipitation \(P\) is partitioned by wet-bulb or air temperature thresholds into snowfall \(P_{\mathrm{snow}}\) and liquid rain \(P_{\mathrm{rain}}\) (\(P = P_{\mathrm{snow}} + P_{\mathrm{rain}}\)). Given net snowpack heat input \(Q_{\mathrm{net}}\) [W m\(^{-2}\)] and latent heat of fusion \(L_f\) (get_physical_constant("latent_heat_fusion")), potential melt \(M_{\mathrm{pot}} = \max(Q_{\mathrm{net}}, 0)/L_f\) is bounded by available solid storage and liquid-water holding capacity, satisfying the exact per-step mass ledger

\[ \Delta W_{\mathrm{snow}} = \left(P_{\mathrm{snow}} + F_{\mathrm{refreeze}} - M_{\mathrm{snow}} - E_{\mathrm{sub}}\right)\Delta t, \]

where \(\Delta W_{\mathrm{snow}}\) is committed via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True) and snow_melt_flux (\(M_{\mathrm{snow}}\)) and rain_flux (\(P_{\mathrm{rain}}\)) are emitted as REPLACE boundary fluxes.

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.snow.albedo.SnowAlbedo (Level 1) is a read-only observation map computing broadband snow surface albedo \(\alpha_{\mathrm{snow}} \in [\alpha_{\min}, \alpha_{\max}]\) from snow age and near-freezing metamorphism decay rates without modifying W_{\mathrm{snow}}.

Soil-water retention, bucket storage, and Richards vadose flow

van Genuchten retention observation (SoilWaterRetention, Level 1)

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.soil_moisture.retention.SoilWaterRetention (Level 1) evaluates the equilibrium van Genuchten (1980) constitutive curve mapping volumetric water content \(\theta\) [m\(^3\) m\(^{-3}\)] to soil matric potential \(\psi\) [MPa] without advancing water storage:

\[ S_e = \operatorname{clip}\!\left(\frac{\theta - \theta_r}{\theta_s - \theta_r},\; S_{e,\min},\; 1\right), \qquad h(S_e) = -\frac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{VG}}}\left(S_e^{-1/m} - 1\right)^{1/n}, \qquad m = 1 - \frac{1}{n}, \]
\[ \psi = 10^{-6}\,\rho_w g\,h(S_e) \le 0\quad [\mathrm{MPa}]. \]

soil_water_potential is emitted via REPLACE for downstream plant-water-stress and stomatal consumers.

Root-zone bucket closure and 1D Richards unsaturated flow

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.soil_moisture.bucket.BucketSoilMoisture (Level 3) evolves single-layer root-zone storage \(S_w = \rho_w Z_r \theta\) [kg m\(^{-2}\)] under infiltration \(I\), evapotranspiration extraction \(E_{\mathrm{ET}}\), gravity drainage \(Q_{\mathrm{drain}}(\theta)\), and saturation capacity \(S_{w,\max} = \rho_w Z_r \theta_s\) (Manabe, 1969):

\[ S_{w,\mathrm{raw}} = S_w + \left(I - E_{\mathrm{ET}} - Q_{\mathrm{drain}}\right)\Delta t, \qquad Q_{\mathrm{sat,ex}} = \frac{\max(S_{w,\mathrm{raw}} - S_{w,\max},\; 0)}{\Delta t}, \]

so accepted storage increment \(\Delta S_w\), drainage, and saturation-excess overflow close to machine precision: \(\Delta S_w - (I - E_{\mathrm{ET}} - Q_{\mathrm{drain}} - Q_{\mathrm{sat,ex}})\Delta t = 0\).

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.soil_moisture.richards.RichardsSoilMoisture (Level 3) solves the multi-layer vertical mixed-form Richards equation (Richards, 1931; Celia et al., 1990) with Mualem-van Genuchten unsaturated hydraulic conductivity \(K(S_e) = K_{\mathrm{sat}} S_e^{\ell}\left[1 - (1 - S_e^{1/m})^m\right]^2\):

\[ \frac{\partial \theta}{\partial t} = -\frac{\partial q_z}{\partial z} - s_{\mathrm{root}}(z), \qquad q_z = -K(\theta)\left(\frac{\partial h(\theta)}{\partial z} + 1\right), \]

in discrete cochain form \(\dot{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_h = -D_h \mathbf{q}_h + G_h \mathbf{u}_h\) with symmetric positive-semidefinite face-conductance operator \(\star_K = \star_K^{\mathsf{T}} \succeq 0\).

Single-writer ownership rule: BucketSoilMoisture, RichardsSoilMoisture, and pedosphere relic.scientific.pedosphere.transport.SoilWaterTransportFunctor.SoilWaterTransportFunctor (Level 3, which emits full next-state soil_moisture via REPLACE) are mutually exclusive owners of volumetric soil moisture. A valid simulator graph registers at most one soil-moisture state writer and routes cross-sphere fluxes through PedosphereInterfaceMapper.

Surface runoff and hybrid event-driven Hortonian ponding

Surface runoff partitioning and liquid-input modes

relic.scientific.hydrosphere.runoff.surface.SurfaceRunoff (Level 3) partitions liquid surface water input rate \(P_{\mathrm{in}}\) [kg m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\)] into overland runoff \(Q_{\mathrm{surf}}\) and soil infiltration \(I\) satisfying exact flux conservation:

\[ P_{\mathrm{in}} = Q_{\mathrm{surf}} + I, \qquad Q_{\mathrm{surf}} \ge 0,\quad I \ge 0. \]

To prevent snowpack double counting when coupled with SnowPack, SurfaceRunoff requires an explicit surface_water_input_source selection:

  • "precipitation_flux": snow-free mode reading total precipitation_flux (\(P_{\mathrm{in}} = P\));

  • "rain_flux_plus_snow_melt_flux": snow-coupled mode reading liquid throughfall plus snowmelt (\(P_{\mathrm{in}} = P_{\mathrm{rain}} + M_{\mathrm{snow}}\)).

Supported constitutive partitioning closures include USDA-SCS Curve Number event abstraction, Hortonian infiltration-capacity excess \(Q_{\mathrm{surf}} = \max(P_{\mathrm{in}} - f_c(\theta), 0)\), Dunne saturation-excess runoff over variable contributing area \(f_{\mathrm{sat}}(\theta)\), and combined infiltration- plus saturation-excess routing.

Hybrid Hortonian ponding event detection and overland recession

When transient storm-scale ponding topology transitions are resolved explicitly (for example alongside MarkedPoissonRainfallFunctor), RELIC pairs two Level 2 Functors in relic.scientific.hydrosphere.runoff.surface_ponding (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapters 19 and 27):

  1. Guard evaluation and topology intent (HortonianPondingEventFunctor, Level 2): Reads cumulative stochastic_rainfall_depth \(H_n\) [mm] and its own replay-critical module extra state \(H_{n-1}\) (persisted through PyTorch get_extra_state / set_extra_state for deterministic checkpoint/restart) to form the step rainfall depth increment \(\Delta H_n = H_n - H_{n-1}\) and Hortonian infiltration-excess depth

    \[E_n = \max\!\left(0,\; \Delta H_n - I_{\max}\,\frac{\Delta t}{3600}\right)\quad [\mathrm{mm}],\]

    where \(I_{\max}\) [mm hr\(^{-1}\)] is maximum infiltration capacity. Given active ponding indicator \(a \in \{0, 1\}\) and current ponded depth \(h_n\) [mm], hysteretic threshold guards (\(E_{\mathrm{on}} > 0\), \(h_{\mathrm{off}} \ge 0\)) emit typed relic.core.state.types.ExternalIntent topology requests ("ponding_onset" when \(a = 0\) and \(\max E_n \ge E_{\mathrm{on}}\); "ponding_cessation" when \(a = 1\), \(\max E_n = 0\), and \(\max h_n \le h_{\mathrm{off}}\)), which the simulator commits between steps via Simulator.apply_topology_transition.

  2. Exact linear-reservoir ponding evolution (SurfacePondingFunctor, Level 2): Advances surface ponded water depth \(h_n\) [mm] over recession timescale \(\tau > 0\) [s] via the exact analytical exponential sub-flow:

    \[h_{n+1} = (h_n + E_n)\exp\!\left(-\frac{\Delta t}{\tau}\right), \qquad q_n = (h_n + E_n) - h_{n+1},\]

    emitting \(\Delta h_n = h_{n+1} - h_n\) via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True) and step runoff depth \(q_n\) / rate \(q_n / \Delta t\) via REPLACE. By construction, the step ponding mass-balance residual \((h_{n+1} - h_n) - E_n + q_n = 0\) vanishes to floating-point roundoff for every \(\Delta t > 0\).

Subsurface stormflow, vadose-aquifer exchange, and groundwater

  1. Subsurface lateral stormflow (SubsurfaceRunoff, Level 3): relic.scientific.hydrosphere.runoff.subsurface.SubsurfaceRunoff computes topographic-slope lateral interflow above low-permeability horizons as a monotone function of drainable water above field capacity, \(Q_{\mathrm{sub}} = k_{\mathrm{sub}}\,\tan\beta_{\mathrm{topo}}\,\max(\theta - \theta_{\mathrm{fc}}, 0)^b\) (Beven and Kirkby, 1979).

  2. Vertical percolation (VerticalPercolationTransport, Level 3) and capillary rise (CapillaryRiseTransport, Level 3): VerticalPercolationTransport routes gravity-driven free drainage \(Q_{\mathrm{perc}} = K(\theta)\) downward from the bottom vadose layer into groundwater recharge (ACCUMULATE storage transfer, conserving total vadose-plus-aquifer water mass). Conversely, CapillaryRiseTransport routes upward matric-suction flux from a shallow water table \(z_{\mathrm{wt}}\) into an unsaturated root zone when \(\psi(\theta_{\mathrm{bot}})\) lies below hydrostatic equilibrium, bounded strictly by available aquifer storage and receiving pore capacity.

  3. Unconfined aquifer dynamics (GroundwaterDynamics, Level 3): relic.scientific.hydrosphere.groundwater.dynamics.GroundwaterDynamics advances unconfined aquifer water storage \(S_{\mathrm{gw}}\) [kg m\(^{-2}\)] and water-table depth \(z_{\mathrm{wt}}\) with specific yield \(S_y\) and linear or nonlinear baseflow recession \(Q_{\mathrm{base}}(S_{\mathrm{gw}})\) (Niu et al., 2007):

    \[\frac{\mathrm{d}S_{\mathrm{gw}}}{\mathrm{d}t} = R_{\mathrm{perc}} - C_{\mathrm{cap}} - Q_{\mathrm{base}}(S_{\mathrm{gw}}) - Q_{\mathrm{pump}}, \qquad \Delta z_{\mathrm{wt}} = -\frac{\Delta S_{\mathrm{gw}}}{\rho_w S_y},\]

    closing the coupled subsurface hydrological ledger \(\Delta S_{\mathrm{gw}} - (R_{\mathrm{perc}} - C_{\mathrm{cap}} - Q_{\mathrm{base}} - Q_{\mathrm{pump}})\Delta t = 0\).

  • Celia, M. A., Bouloutas, E. T., and Zarba, R. L. (1990). A general mass-conservative numerical solution for the unsaturated flow equation. Water Resources Research, 26, 1483-1496.
